phases.title: Recovery integrity and agent handoff
phases.goal: Preserve and index the entire recovery, sanitize remote credentials and publish a reproducible agent handoff.
acceptance: Every original recovery file is mapped; duplicates have one resource object
No raw service token, webhook or connection password is exported
Repository checks pass on a clean checkout

tasks.title: Verify full source and resource coverage
Review credential redactions and unchanged source hashes
Provide canonical-versus-variant and resource maps
Create phase/task/feature dependency ledgers
Run integrity, security and navigation checks
Publish to main without force and verify remote state

phases.title: Apple runtime and differential test laboratory
phases.goal: Run recovered CSharp checks on standalone iPad/iPhone simulators and retain honest device AOT evidence.
acceptance: A nonzero build exit or missing result file fails CI
The required assertion count and input hash are checked
AOT compilation is not physical-device execution
100000-byte compression failure remains visible until original-versus-recovery comparison resolves it

tasks.title: Reproduce native startup and distinguish signature failure from managed failure
Validate ad-hoc signatures for the app and nested native libraries
Capture native startup, managed Main and FinishedLaunching markers
Run original-binary math goldens and vector/material checks on iOS
Turn compression mismatches into explicit differential compatibility failures
blockers: Original-binary compression comparison needs the contained Windows reference (B-001)

tasks.title: Add iPad/iPhone device profiles and collect unsigned Release AOT warnings

phases.title: Contained Windows oracle and fixture corpus
phases.goal: Establish authoritative Windows behavior in a D:-contained environment and obtain representative PC projects.
blockers: No D:-contained Windows reference VM/image or complete licensed runtime/account/catalog supplied
acceptance: No VM/image/license/account is assumed available
The public item-4 library fixture is not a PC portfolio oracle
Do not use embedded credentials or execute vendor-account requests
Each oracle records PC build, input hash, edit steps and expected outputs

tasks.title: Inventory missing runtime, licensing, catalog state and user-created projects
Prepare a contained Windows reference VM with its disk, profile and tools on D:
Hash the original installers and distinguish altered loose-executable behavior
Acquire the twenty planned fixture families with provenance and version labels
Capture Windows open-edit-regenerate-save-reopen results and UI images
Publish oracle fields, geometry outputs, tolerances and failure cases

phases.title: Portable domain and graph contracts
phases.goal: Extract existing algorithms and graph state into portable CSharp projects with explicit platform boundaries.
acceptance: Portable projects reference no Rhino or Windows UI DLL
Default, non-default, boundary and invalid inputs have explicit cases
Serialized type identity survives namespace/assembly changes through tested mappings
Windows native declarations compiling successfully do not count as functioning reuse

tasks.title: Create Domain, Graph and Domain.Tests projects
Classify adopted methods as unchanged, adapted, generated data or replacement
Define GUID/parameter identity, units, graph links and immutable snapshots
Port validation, numerical/material helpers and undoable parameter changes
Replace Windows/COM/native/service assumptions with typed real boundaries
Run differential edge-case tests and record retained/changed/new code

phases.title: Loss-preserving PC document codecs
phases.goal: Read and write portfolios, CSG graphs and legacy records while retaining unknown data and editable identities.
acceptance: Item-4 edit 4.38 to 4.48 preserves 240 other records and 73 other numbers
No-op preservation, unknown nodes, corrupt CRC, truncation and duplicate labels are tested
Cached volume/preview retention is not geometry regeneration
Unsupported future records never cause silent data removal or overwrite

tasks.title: Create Documents and Documents.Tests with an independent fixture reader
Implement bounded envelopes, chunk tables, CRC and record version handling
Implement portfolio XML, paired GUID filenames, sidecars, previews and history
Map all 654 serializer identities and inherited reader/writer/version behavior
Implement no-op save, one-parameter edits and explicit migration policy
Verify edited PC-to-iOS-to-PC reopening and fail-closed future formats

phases.title: Offline CAD backend and native bridge
phases.goal: Prove a real on-device geometry backend against the recovered operation requirements.
acceptance: Missing operations remain blocked; dummy meshes and success-returning stubs cannot pass
No network geometry compute is permitted
Independent CAD SDK source is not claimed as recovered code
Repeated failure, cancellation and handle disposal do not leak memory

tasks.title: Map all 315 kernel/wrapper call families to required semantics
Evaluate iOS-capable kernels using actual sweeps, trims, booleans, meshing and archive fixtures
Record the backend decision with distribution/license prerequisites and gaps
Implement a versioned C ABI with opaque handles, ownership and typed errors
Implement CSharp adapters for representative curve/surface/solid/mesh operations
Compare PC/iOS topology, units, orientation, tolerances, cancellation and memory

phases.title: One complete jewelry vertical slice
phases.goal: Open a real design, edit it, regenerate locally, save it and reopen it editably on PC.
acceptance: A byte patch, screenshot or cached mesh is not this milestone
Graph, geometry, measurements, previews and manufacturing exports are checked separately
The edited design survives offline force-quit/relaunch
Use this measured slice to revise estimates; do not reuse withdrawn LOC guesses

tasks.title: Select a representative builder and a Windows oracle fixture
Map original parameters, call graph, validation and legacy serializer dependencies
Adapt the recovered algorithm to real graph/document/geometry contracts
Build a minimal touch editor with a named parameter and regenerated viewport
Implement actual save/reopen, undo/redo and atomic failure rollback
Compare Windows and iOS outputs and record measured adaptation effort

phases.title: All builders and legacy graph behavior
phases.goal: Port every declared builder identity and legacy behavior in bounded auditable batches.
acceptance: Every builder is verified or explicitly blocked
Do not silently replace old algorithms with their newest variants
A class declaration or constructor registration is insufficient
Reserved/expired nodes preserve expected error behavior

tasks.title: Partition all 619 builder rows by namespace, dependency family and legacy status
Map a bounded batch of input/output channels and original algorithms
Port current and legacy implementations with stable GUID/version dispatch
Test limits, non-defaults, invalid geometry and parameter combinations
Test mixed legacy/current graphs, ordering, invalidation and cancellation
Attach fixtures, Windows comparisons, iOS results and review to each builder row

phases.title: Viewport materials rendering and try-on
phases.goal: Implement offline interactive and final rendering with objective visual comparisons.
acceptance: Fixed camera/light/material scenes have reference images and thresholds
A generic shiny material is not gemstone parity
Missing original resources remain explicit gaps
No rendering server or mandatory online asset fetch is used

tasks.title: Map camera, selection, display modes, materials, lights and try-on behavior
Implement geometry upload, picking, navigation and frame synchronization
Implement gemstone/metal mapping, lighting, environments and backgrounds
Map deduplicated resources to semantic assets and supported mobile formats
Implement local final rendering, image export and try-on calibration
Benchmark fixed scenes, selection, memory and thermal behavior on real devices

phases.title: Complete native touch interface
phases.goal: Recreate every recovered UI workflow and state transition for iPad and iPhone.
acceptance: Every command/event maps to a test or an explicit original-source gap
No static placeholder panel or empty action satisfies a workflow
Core flows work offline with state restoration and actionable errors
Functionality survives compact layouts; literal desktop pixels/mouse behavior are not presumed

tasks.title: Map 68 UI groups, 317 public commands, 113 XAML files and 771 hookups
Implement native navigation, selection, property editing and catalog surfaces in CSharp/UIKit
Implement customize/freehand, dialogs, validation, orders and saved designs
Resolve dormant commands, empty handlers and ambiguous bindings with reference evidence
Implement undo/redo, gestures, appropriate Pencil/keyboard support, accessibility and localization
Run interaction and screenshot cases across device sizes and orientations

phases.title: Catalog pricing projects quotes and reports
phases.goal: Implement local data and commerce workflows while accounting explicitly for server-only capabilities.
acceptance: No complete account-specific catalog is assumed recovered
Offline substitutions are not silently labeled identical live services
No embedded credential, fake activation or entitlement bypass is used
Quote outputs are checked against versioned expected financial results

tasks.title: Map schemas, profiles, catalog/component relationships and asset references
Implement local ingestion, indexing, filters, categories and component availability
Implement project/customer administration, portfolios, quotes and reports
Implement reproducible price snapshots, options, units, rounding and currency
Record live supplier/account/service actions as explicit scope decisions
Compare offline, stale/missing data, migration and report output to PC fixtures

phases.title: Stored scripts and AOT-safe execution
phases.goal: Preserve supported stored-script behavior with an offline iOS-compatible execution strategy.
acceptance: Do not assume CodeDom/csc.exe or arbitrary Windows dependencies run on iOS
Never execute recovered scripts on the Windows host during setup
Unsupported scripts retain their original data and fail explicitly
Script failures cannot silently delete nodes or corrupt saved designs

tasks.title: Inventory CSScript source/configuration, arguments, ref/out outputs and geometry calls
Define supported script APIs and precise unsupported Windows/native operations
Evaluate precompiled factories or a bounded interpreter against actual scripts
Implement typed binding, explicit registries and AOT/trim metadata preservation
Implement execution budgets, cancellation, errors and transactional rollback
Round-trip script source/configuration and compare supported outputs

phases.title: Manufacturing export and hardware contracts
phases.goal: Produce correct document/manufacturing outputs and explicit mobile hardware integration contracts.
acceptance: STL/3DM export does not substitute for editable CounterSketch projects
Selected-only and full-document exports have separate cases
Disconnected hardware and unsupported formats fail precisely
Unavailable Windows plugins are never claimed working

tasks.title: Map import/export, mesh, support-generation and printer entry points
Implement object inclusion, units, transforms, normals and orientation policies
Implement required real CAD/mesh/image formats and metadata mapping
Implement required support-generation and mesh-repair behavior
Record tested mobile equivalents or blockers for Windows/COM/native plugin paths
Independently reopen exports and verify dimensions, topology and watertightness

phases.title: Lifecycle persistence performance and packaging
phases.goal: Make the complete offline app reliable under mobile lifecycle and resource constraints.
acceptance: Force-quit during save preserves the last valid document
Physical performance is measured, not inferred from compile success
Offline startup requires no catalog/cache fetch
Local Windows caches/tools remain confined to D:

tasks.title: Implement atomic save, autosave, history, crash recovery and storage limits
Integrate Files import/export and app-local libraries without mandatory cloud services
Implement suspend/resume, rotation, cancellation and state restoration
Benchmark large graphs, repeated edits, undo, meshes, render memory and thermal load
Resolve AOT/trim warnings using real resource/reflection/serialization cases
Create reproducible signed-device and simulator build/distribution instructions

phases.title: Full interoperability and feature acceptance
phases.goal: Close every required feature/type row with reproducible PC/iOS/PC evidence.
acceptance: 654 serializer rows and 619 builder rows overlap; they are not independent feature counts
No row is verified solely by a class declaration or build
Offline adaptations and unavailable services remain visibly distinct from parity
A reviewer can reproduce each accepted row from its fixture and command

tasks.title: Run the twenty-family corpus across supported PC versions and record branches
Exercise no-op and edited interchanges with histories, scripts and sidecars
Compare graph identity, parameters, geometry, units, materials, previews and exports separately
Exercise corrupt data, unknown nodes, unsupported versions and mixed legacy graphs
Audit all UI/CAD/PC/serializer/builder rows for stale or missing evidence
Publish the supported-version matrix and unresolved blockers

phases.title: Physical-device release and parity sign-off
phases.goal: Release only when the recorded functional, visual, compatibility and offline scope is supported by evidence.
acceptance: Signing/distribution accounts are real external prerequisites
No full parity claim while a required row is blocked or static-only
Supported scope excludes untested future PC versions and unavailable live services
Release artifacts are tested independently of development builds

tasks.title: Freeze PC versions, hardware matrix, fixture hashes and the feature contract
Run all supported workflows on physical iPad and iPhone without network access
Verify accessibility, localization, upgrades, startup, storage and recovery
Resolve or withhold claims for missing catalog/script/render/hardware capabilities
Perform fresh code/security/dependency review and signed distribution validation
Publish exact release evidence, known limits and reproducible build instructions
